business_glossary_term: Runway Safety Area (RSA) Width in Feet

business_glossary_term: Runway Visibility Value (RVV) Reciprocal End in Feet

business_glossary_term: Visual Glide Slope Indicator Base End Type

business_glossary_term: Visual Glide Slope Indicator Reciprocal End Type

Condition rating for bridge bearings on a scale of 0-9. Evaluates the condition and functionality of bearing assemblies that support the superstructure.
Date on which inspection data was entered into the Bridge Management System (BMS). Tracks data processing timeliness.
NBIS condition rating for the channel and channel protection on a scale of 0-9. Evaluates the condition of the waterway channel and erosion protection measures.
Indicates whether bridge closure is recommended based on critical structural deficiencies or safety concerns. True if closure is recommended.
Assessment of condition change since the previous inspection: improved, unchanged, deteriorated, or significantly deteriorated. Tracks condition trends.
Indicates whether corrosion was observed during the inspection on steel or reinforced concrete elements. True if corrosion is present.
Severity of observed corrosion: none, light, moderate, severe, or critical. Classifies the extent and impact of corrosion on structural members.
Indicates whether cracking was observed in structural members during the inspection. True if cracks are present in concrete or steel components.
Type of cracking observed: flexural, shear, fatigue, thermal, shrinkage, or other. Classifies the crack type to determine cause and structural significance.
NBIS condition rating for culverts on a scale of 0-9. Assesses the structural and functional condition of culvert structures.
Indicates whether debris accumulation was observed at the bridge, particularly at piers or in the waterway. True if debris is present.

NBIS condition rating for the bridge deck on a scale of 0-9, where 9 is excellent condition and 0 is failed condition. Assesses the condition of the bridge deck surface and structural integrity.
NBIS rating for deck geometry adequacy on a scale of 0-9. Evaluates whether the deck width, alignment, and geometry meet current standards.
Primary defect code identifying the most significant defect observed during inspection. Uses standardized defect coding system for classification.
Secondary defect code identifying additional significant defects observed during inspection. Captures the second most critical defect.
Description of the extent or spread of the defect across the structure, including measurements, affected area, and progression since previous inspection.
Detailed description of the location of observed defects on the bridge structure, including span number, member identification, and specific location details.
Severity classification of the primary defect: minor, moderate, severe, or critical. Indicates the urgency and impact of the identified defect.
Indicates whether concrete delamination was observed during the inspection. True if separation of concrete layers is detected.
Condition rating for bridge drainage systems on a scale of 0-9. Evaluates the condition and effectiveness of deck drainage and scupper systems.
Indicates whether emergency notification to management or regulatory authorities is required based on critical findings. True if immediate escalation is needed.
Description of specialized equipment used during the inspection (e.g., snooper truck, drone, ultrasonic testing equipment). Documents inspection tools and technology.
Estimated cost in dollars for recommended repairs or actions. Provides preliminary cost estimate for budgeting and prioritization purposes.
Condition rating for expansion joints on a scale of 0-9. Assesses the condition of joints that accommodate bridge movement due to temperature and loading.
Indicates whether repairs or actions recommended from this inspection are eligible for federal aid funding. True if federal funding may be available.
Textual summary of key findings, deficiencies, or notable observations from the inspection. Provides an executive summary of inspection results.
Detailed description of fracture critical members, their location, condition, and any findings from hands-on inspection of FCM components.
Indicates whether the bridge contains fracture critical members (FCM) that require special inspection. True if the bridge has tension members whose failure would cause collapse.
Compliance status of the inspection relative to regulatory requirements and scheduled due dates: compliant, overdue, or early. Tracks adherence to inspection schedules.
The date on which the bridge or structure inspection was performed. This is the actual field inspection date when the bridge was physically examined.
Total duration of the inspection in hours, from start to completion of field work. Used for resource planning and cost tracking.
The required frequency of inspection in months based on bridge condition, type, and regulatory requirements. Determines the inspection cycle for the bridge.
Primary method used to conduct the inspection (e.g., visual, hands-on, instrumented, remote). Documents the inspection approach and techniques employed.
General notes and observations from the inspection that do not fit into other structured fields. Captures additional context and inspector observations.
The name of the organization or contractor that performed the inspection. Identifies whether the inspection was conducted by NCDOT staff or an external contractor.
Date on which the formal inspection report was completed and finalized. May differ from the inspection date if report preparation takes time.
Unique report number or document identifier for the formal inspection report. Links the database record to the official inspection report document.
Current status of the inspection record: scheduled, in progress, completed, under review, or finalized. Tracks inspection workflow status.
Names of additional team members who participated in the inspection. Documents the full inspection team composition for accountability and quality assurance purposes.
The type or category of inspection performed (e.g., routine, fracture-critical, underwater, special, in-depth, damage). This is the descriptive text representation of the inspection classification.
The expiration date of the inspector's certification or license. Used to ensure inspector qualifications are current at the time of inspection.
The certification or license number of the lead inspector who performed the inspection. Validates inspector qualifications and regulatory compliance.
Load level that can be safely supported for an indefinite period of time. Represents the load capacity for long-term structural integrity.
Condition rating for bridge lighting systems on a scale of 0-9. Assesses the condition and functionality of bridge lighting infrastructure.
Indicates whether load restrictions are recommended based on inspection findings and structural capacity analysis. True if posting is recommended.
Date on which inspection data was submitted to the National Bridge Inventory. Tracks federal reporting compliance.
Indicates whether this inspection data was submitted to the National Bridge Inventory (NBI) database. True if data was reported to FHWA.
The date by which the next inspection must be completed based on regulatory requirements, bridge condition, and inspection frequency. Calculated or assigned date for scheduling future inspections.
Maximum permissible live load to which the structure may be subjected for routine use. Represents the load level for normal traffic conditions.
Overall NBIS condition rating for the structure, typically the lowest rating among deck, superstructure, and substructure. Provides a summary assessment of overall bridge condition.
Condition of protective paint or coating on steel members: excellent, good, fair, poor, or failed. Assesses the effectiveness of corrosion protection systems.
Number of photographs taken and associated with the inspection record. Quantifies the extent of photographic documentation.
Indicates whether photographic documentation was captured during the inspection. True if photos were taken to document conditions.
Maximum vehicle weight limit in tons if the bridge is posted for load restrictions. Specifies the maximum safe vehicle weight allowed on the bridge.
Current posting status of the bridge based on load capacity analysis: open (no restrictions), posted (weight restrictions), or closed. Indicates whether load restrictions are in effect.
Date of the previous inspection for comparison and trend analysis. Enables tracking of condition changes over time.
Comments from the quality assurance reviewer regarding inspection quality, findings, or required corrections. Documents QA feedback.
Date on which the quality assurance review was completed. Tracks QA process timeline.
Indicates whether quality assurance review of the inspection is required based on bridge criticality or inspection findings. True if QA review is needed.
Status of the quality assurance review: approved, approved with comments, rejected, or pending revision. Indicates QA outcome.
Name of the quality assurance reviewer who reviewed the inspection report and findings. Documents QA accountability.
Condition rating for bridge railings on a scale of 0-9. Evaluates the condition and safety adequacy of bridge railings and barriers.
Primary recommended action based on inspection findings: monitor, repair, rehabilitate, replace, or close. Specifies the recommended response to inspection findings.
Detailed description of the recommended action, including scope of work, specific repairs needed, and justification based on inspection findings.
Priority level for the recommended action: low, medium, high, or critical. Indicates the urgency of implementing the recommended action.
Detailed description of any immediate safety concerns identified during inspection, including nature of the hazard and recommended immediate actions.
Indicates whether immediate safety concerns were identified during the inspection. True if conditions pose an immediate risk to public safety.
Rating of scour condition at bridge foundations on a scale of 0-9. Assesses the current state of scour at piers and abutments.

Indicator of scour criticality: Y (scour critical), N (not scour critical), U (unknown), or T (scour critical with temporary monitoring). Identifies bridges at risk of foundation failure due to scour.
Detailed description of scour vulnerability, observed scour conditions, and any countermeasures in place. Documents scour risk assessment and mitigation measures.
Measured settlement in inches, if applicable. Quantifies the amount of vertical displacement observed at foundations or approaches.
Indicates whether foundation or approach settlement was observed during the inspection. True if vertical displacement of foundations or approaches is detected.
Indicates whether concrete spalling was observed during the inspection. True if concrete surface deterioration with loss of material is present.
Detailed narrative evaluation of the structural condition, including assessment of load-carrying capacity, structural integrity, and any concerns identified during inspection.
NBIS condition rating for the bridge substructure on a scale of 0-9. Assesses the condition of piers, abutments, and other supporting elements below the superstructure.
NBIS condition rating for the bridge superstructure on a scale of 0-9. Evaluates the condition of the main load-carrying members above the substructure.
Ambient temperature in degrees Fahrenheit at the time of inspection. Temperature conditions can affect material behavior and inspection observations.
Indicates whether traffic control measures were required to safely conduct the inspection. True if lane closures or traffic management was needed.
Type of traffic control implemented during the inspection (e.g., lane closure, full closure, flagging, temporary signals). Documents traffic management approach.
Minimum horizontal clearance under the bridge in feet. Measures the width available for traffic or waterway passage beneath the bridge.
Minimum vertical clearance under the bridge in feet. Critical for determining whether vehicles or vessels can safely pass under the structure.
Detailed findings from underwater inspection, including condition of submerged piers, footings, scour conditions, and debris accumulation below the waterline.
Indicates whether an underwater inspection was performed as part of this inspection event. True if submerged portions of the bridge were inspected.
Method used for underwater inspection (e.g., diver inspection, remote operated vehicle, sonar). Documents the technique used to inspect submerged bridge components.
Indicates whether vegetation growth was observed on the bridge structure or approaches. True if vegetation is present that may affect drainage or structural integrity.
NBIS rating for waterway adequacy on a scale of 0-9. Assesses whether the waterway opening is sufficient to pass expected flood flows without causing excessive backwater.
Description of weather conditions at the time of inspection (e.g., clear, cloudy, rain, fog). Weather can affect inspection visibility and findings.
Unique identifier for the bridge inspection type. Primary key for the inspection type lookup table.
Description of special access equipment or methods required to perform this inspection type (e.g., snooper truck, ladder, boat, diving equipment, rope access, traffic control, lane closure).

Indicates whether this inspection type is currently active and available for use in inspection scheduling and planning. Inactive types are retained for historical reference but not used for new inspections.

Types of bridge structures for which this inspection type is applicable or required (e.g., all bridges, fracture critical bridges only, movable bridges, suspension bridges, truss bridges, bridges over water).

Bridge construction material types for which this inspection type is applicable (e.g., steel, concrete, timber, composite). Some inspection types are material-specific (e.g., fracture critical inspections primarily for steel structures).
Indicates whether inspection results from this type are integrated into the NCDOT Bridge Management System for condition assessment, prioritization, and lifecycle planning.

High-level category classifying the inspection type by scheduling nature: scheduled (routine, periodic), unscheduled (damage, post-event), special (fracture critical, underwater), regulatory (compliance-driven), or emergency (immediate response).

Specific certifications or training required for inspectors to perform this inspection type (e.g., NBIS Bridge Inspector Certification, Fracture Critical Inspector Training, Underwater Bridge Inspection Certification, NDE Level II Certification).

Indicates whether this inspection type has potential to identify conditions that could result in immediate bridge closure or load posting (typically true for damage inspections, special inspections, and fracture critical inspections).
Short alphanumeric code representing the inspection type (e.g., ROUTINE, SPECIAL, FRACTURE, UNDERWATER, DAMAGE). Used for system integration and reporting.
Indicates whether results from this inspection type directly impact the official NBI condition ratings (deck rating, superstructure rating, substructure rating, culvert rating).
Upper bound of typical cost range in USD to perform this inspection type for an average bridge structure. Used for budgeting and resource allocation.
Lower bound of typical cost range in USD to perform this inspection type for an average bridge structure. Used for budgeting and resource allocation.
Detailed description of the inspection type, including its purpose, scope, and when it should be performed according to NBIS standards and NCDOT policies.

Specific documentation requirements for this inspection type beyond standard reporting (e.g., photographic documentation of all members, sketches of damage locations, NDE test results, underwater video footage, drone imagery).
Date when this inspection type definition was retired or superseded. Null if currently active.
Date when this inspection type definition became effective and available for use in NCDOT bridge inspection program.

Description of environmental factors or restrictions that must be considered when performing this inspection type (e.g., protected species nesting periods, water quality concerns, noise restrictions, vegetation clearing limitations).
Typical estimated duration in hours to complete this inspection type for an average bridge structure. Used for resource planning and scheduling.

business_glossary_term: Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) Notification Required Flag
description: Indicates whether FHWA must be notified of inspection findings from this type (typically true for critical findings, bridge closures, or significant structural deficiencies).

Type of follow-up inspection typically required or recommended based on findings from this inspection type (e.g., routine inspection may trigger special inspection, damage inspection may trigger in-depth inspection).

Standard inspection frequency interval in months as defined by NBIS or NCDOT policy. For example, routine inspections are typically 24 months, fracture critical inspections may be 24 months, and underwater inspections may be 60 months.
Inspection depth level as defined by AASHTO Manual for Bridge Evaluation: Level 1 (visual), Level 2 (detailed visual with access), Level 3 (highly detailed with NDE), Level 4 (laboratory testing).
Date when this inspection type definition was last reviewed or updated in the system.
Indicates whether findings from this inspection type may trigger a load rating analysis or update to the bridge operating and inventory ratings.
Maximum allowable frequency interval in months for this inspection type, representing the longest permissible time between inspections under NBIS or NCDOT standards before non-compliance occurs.
Minimum allowable frequency interval in months for this inspection type, representing the most frequent inspection cycle permitted under NBIS or NCDOT standards.
Full descriptive name of the inspection type (e.g., Routine Inspection, Special Inspection, Fracture Critical Member Inspection, Underwater Inspection, Damage Inspection, In-Depth Inspection).

business_glossary_term: National Bridge Inventory (NBI) Submission Required Flag
description: Indicates whether results from this inspection type must be submitted to the National Bridge Inventory database maintained by FHWA.

business_glossary_term: National Bridge Inspection Standards (NBIS) Required Flag
description: Indicates whether this inspection type is mandated by federal NBIS regulations (23 CFR 650). True for routine, fracture critical, and underwater inspections; false for optional or state-specific inspection types.

List of non-destructive evaluation methods that may be employed during this inspection type (e.g., ultrasonic testing, magnetic particle testing, dye penetrant testing, ground penetrating radar, acoustic emission testing).

Indicates whether special permits are required to perform this inspection type (e.g., waterway work permits for underwater inspections, traffic control permits for lane closures, environmental permits for work in sensitive areas).
Indicates whether photographic documentation is mandatory for this inspection type as part of the inspection record.
Priority classification for scheduling and resource allocation: critical (immediate safety concern), high (regulatory deadline), medium (standard schedule), low (optional or deferred).
Indicates whether public notification is required when this inspection type is performed or when certain findings are identified (e.g., lane closures, bridge closures, load restrictions).

Minimum qualification level required for inspectors performing this inspection type, as defined by NBIS and NCDOT certification standards (e.g., team leader, bridge inspector, fracture critical inspector, underwater inspector, NDE technician).

Level of quality assurance review required for inspection reports of this type: Level 1 (peer review), Level 2 (supervisory review), Level 3 (independent QA team review). Higher risk inspection types require higher QA levels.
Primary regulatory authority or standard that defines or mandates this inspection type (e.g., FHWA NBIS, AASHTO Manual for Bridge Evaluation, NCDOT Bridge Inspection Manual, State Statute).

Standard reporting format or template required for documenting results of this inspection type (e.g., NBI format for routine inspections, detailed narrative report for special inspections, NDE report for non-destructive evaluation).
Indicates whether inspection reports of this type require formal review and approval by a qualified team leader or program manager before finalization.

Assessment of inherent safety risk to inspection personnel performing this inspection type: extreme (underwater, high elevation rope access), high (under-bridge access, confined spaces), moderate (traffic exposure), low (visual from ground).

Defines the extent of the bridge structure covered by this inspection type: full structure (entire bridge), partial structure (selected spans or sections), specific component (deck, superstructure, substructure), underwater only (submerged elements), or fracture critical only (FCM members).

Description of any seasonal restrictions or preferred timing for this inspection type (e.g., underwater inspections best performed in summer, avoid winter for detailed inspections due to ice, environmental restrictions during nesting season).
Indicates whether specialized equipment beyond standard inspection tools is required for this inspection type (e.g., underwater diving gear, ultrasonic testing equipment, snooper trucks, drones).
Code or name of the inspection type that replaced this inspection type, if applicable. Used to track evolution of inspection standards and practices.
Minimum number of qualified personnel required to safely and effectively perform this inspection type, as defined by NBIS safety standards and NCDOT policy.
Indicates whether traffic control measures (lane closures, flaggers, work zone setup) are typically required to perform this inspection type safely.

Specific event or condition that triggers this inspection type (e.g., hurricane, flood, earthquake, vehicle impact, fire, structural damage report, routine schedule). Applicable primarily to unscheduled and emergency inspection types.
Indicates whether video documentation is required for this inspection type (typically true for underwater inspections and some special inspections).

Indicates whether this inspection type is significantly dependent on favorable weather conditions (e.g., underwater inspections require calm water, detailed visual inspections require good visibility).

Number of traffic incidents (crashes, breakdowns, etc.) occurring in this lane annually.
Measurement of pavement roughness in inches per mile. Lower values indicate smoother pavement. Critical metric for ride quality and HPMS reporting.
Indicates whether this lane is equipped with ITS infrastructure (sensors, cameras, dynamic message signs, etc.).
Type of ITS sensors deployed in this lane (e.g., loop detectors, radar, video detection, bluetooth, RFID).
Date of the most recent condition inspection performed on this lane.
Date of the most recent major rehabilitation work performed on this lane.
Date of the most recent resurfacing or overlay work performed on this lane.
Total length of this lane segment measured in miles.
Current condition of roadway lighting infrastructure serving this lane.
Type of roadway lighting installed for this lane (LED, high pressure sodium, metal halide, none).
Level of Service rating (A through F) indicating traffic flow quality and congestion level. A represents free flow, F represents forced flow/breakdown.
NCDOT maintenance district responsible for this lane (e.g., District 1, District 2, etc.).
Priority level assigned for maintenance activities based on condition assessment and traffic importance (critical, high, medium, low).
Specific maintenance unit or crew responsible for routine maintenance of this lane.
Current condition of the lane markings based on visibility and retroreflectivity assessment.
Measured retroreflectivity of lane markings in millicandelas per lux per square meter (mcd/lx/m²). Indicates nighttime visibility performance.
Type of pavement marking delineating the lane boundaries (solid white, dashed white, solid yellow, dashed yellow, double yellow, none).
Type of median separating opposing traffic flows (barrier, depressed, raised, flush, none). Applicable for lanes adjacent to median.
Width of the median measured in feet. Applicable for lanes adjacent to median.
Name of the Metropolitan Planning Organization with jurisdiction over this lane, if applicable.
Planned date for the next scheduled maintenance activity on this lane.
Indicates whether this lane is part of the National Highway System, which includes roadways important to the nation's economy, defense, and mobility.
Indicates whether noise barriers are present adjacent to this lane for noise mitigation.
Sequential number of the lane within the segment, typically numbered from left to right or median to shoulder.
Age of the current pavement surface in years since last major rehabilitation or reconstruction.
Numerical rating of pavement condition on a scale of 0-100, where 100 represents excellent condition. Used for pavement management and maintenance prioritization.
Maximum hourly traffic volume observed on this lane during peak periods.
Estimated remaining service life of the pavement before major rehabilitation is required, expressed in years.
The route identifier for the highway or roadway containing this lane (e.g., I-40, US-1, NC-55).
Name of the Rural Planning Organization with jurisdiction over this lane, if applicable.
Maximum depth of rutting (wheel path depressions) measured in inches. Indicator of pavement structural distress.
Type of shoulder on the left side of the lane (paved, gravel, turf, none).
Type of shoulder on the right side of the lane (paved, gravel, turf, none).
Width of the left shoulder adjacent to this lane, measured in feet.
Width of the right shoulder adjacent to this lane, measured in feet.
Available stopping sight distance for this lane measured in feet. Critical safety metric.

business_glossary_term: Posted Speed Limit in Miles Per Hour
description: The posted speed limit for this lane in miles per hour (mph).
Current operational status of the lane (active, closed, under construction, planned, decommissioned).
STIP project number associated with this lane for planned improvements or construction.
Banking of the roadway on horizontal curves expressed as a percentage. Used to counteract centrifugal force.
Current condition rating of the lane surface based on visual inspection and condition assessment.
The type of pavement surface material used for this lane (asphalt, concrete, composite, gravel, unpaved).
Indicates whether this lane is part of a toll facility requiring payment for use.
Type of toll rate structure applied to this lane (flat, distance-based, time-of-day, dynamic pricing, none).
The annual average daily traffic volume for trucks and heavy vehicles on this lane.
Percentage of total traffic volume that consists of trucks and heavy vehicles.
Indicates whether this lane is part of a designated truck route for commercial vehicle traffic.
Classification of the lane based on its designated usage (e.g., general purpose, HOV, truck, bus, bike, turn lane, acceleration/deceleration, auxiliary, reversible, shoulder, parking).
Specific restrictions or requirements for using this lane (e.g., HOV 2+, trucks only, no trucks, buses only, time-of-day restrictions).
The width of the lane measured in feet. Standard lane widths typically range from 10 to 12 feet.
Unique identifier for each pavement condition assessment record.
Unique asset identifier for the pavement section in the NCDOT asset management system.
Identifier for the crew or team that performed the pavement condition assessment.
Unique identifier for the pavement section within the route.
Reference identifier linking to photographs taken during the pavement inspection.
The state route number or identifier for the roadway segment being assessed.

business_glossary_term: State Transportation Improvement Program (STIP) Project Identifier
description: Identifier for any STIP project associated with planned improvements to this pavement section.
Average number of vehicles per day traveling on this pavement section over a one-year period.
Percentage of pavement section area affected by alligator (fatigue) cracking, indicating structural failure.
Starting milepost location of the pavement section being assessed.
Severity level of asphalt bleeding where excess binder creates a shiny surface.
Percentage of pavement section area affected by block cracking patterns.
Additional notes or observations recorded by the inspector during the assessment.
North Carolina county code where the pavement section is located.
Name of the North Carolina county where the pavement section is located.
Overall severity level of pavement cracking observed during inspection.
Direction of travel during pavement condition data collection.
Source system or application from which the pavement condition data originated.
The most significant type of pavement distress observed during inspection.
The second most significant type of pavement distress observed during inspection.
NCDOT highway division number responsible for maintaining this pavement section.
Assessment of the pavement drainage system effectiveness.
Total linear feet of cracking along the pavement edge.
Ending milepost location of the pavement section being assessed.
Estimated cost in US dollars to implement the recommended pavement treatment.
Indicates whether this pavement section is eligible for federal funding assistance.
Date when the most recent friction or skid resistance test was performed.
reference: ASTM E274 - Standard Test Method for Skid Resistance

description: FHWA functional classification of the roadway section.
GPS latitude coordinate for the pavement section location.
GPS longitude coordinate for the pavement section location.

business_glossary_term: Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Sample Indicator
description: Indicates whether this section is part of the FHWA HPMS sample for federal reporting.
Date when the pavement condition assessment was performed.
Type of equipment or technology used for the pavement condition assessment.
Method used to conduct the pavement condition assessment (manual walking survey, automated vehicle survey, windshield survey, or detailed distress survey).
Calendar year in which the pavement condition assessment was conducted.
Name of the certified inspector who conducted the pavement condition assessment.
Qualitative rating of ride quality based on IRI value (Very Good: <95, Good: 95-170, Fair: 170-220, Poor: 220-320, Very Poor: >320).
Measurement of pavement roughness in inches per mile, used to assess ride quality and comfort.
Total linear feet of cracks reflecting underlying joint patterns in overlaid pavements.
Total number of through lanes in both directions for the pavement section.
Average width of travel lanes in feet.
Date when the most recent overlay or resurfacing was applied to this section.
Assessment of the pavement's ability to carry traffic loads.
reference: AASHTO Guide for Design of Pavement Structures

description: Total linear feet of longitudinal cracks parallel to the pavement centerline.
NCDOT maintenance unit responsible for this pavement section.
Name of the Metropolitan Planning Organization with jurisdiction over this section, if applicable.
Indicates whether the pavement section is part of the National Highway System.
Percentage of pavement section area that has been patched or repaired.
Number of years since the pavement was originally constructed or last reconstructed.
Qualitative rating category derived from PCI score (Excellent: 85-100, Very Good: 70-85, Good: 55-70, Fair: 40-55, Poor: 25-40, Very Poor: 10-25, Serious: 0-10, Failed: 0).
reference: ASTM D6433 - Standard Practice for Roads and Parking Lots Pavement Condition Index Surveys

description: Numerical rating of pavement condition on a scale of 0-100, where 100 represents excellent condition and 0 represents failed pavement.
reference: ASTM D6433 - Standard Practice for Roads and Parking Lots Pavement Condition Index Surveys

description: Severity level of aggregate polishing that reduces surface friction.
Number of potholes identified within the pavement section.
Subjective rating of pavement serviceability on a scale of 0-5, where 5 represents perfect pavement and 0 represents failed pavement.
reference: AASHTO Guide for Design of Pavement Structures

description: Date when the quality assurance review was completed.
Name of the quality assurance reviewer who validated the assessment data.
Indicates whether this assessment has passed quality assurance review.
Severity level of surface raveling or aggregate loss from the pavement surface.
Recommended maintenance or rehabilitation treatment based on pavement condition assessment.
Current status of the pavement condition assessment record.
Estimated number of years before the pavement will require major rehabilitation or reconstruction.
Subjective assessment of pavement ride quality and smoothness.
Name of the Rural Planning Organization with jurisdiction over this section, if applicable.
Maximum depth of wheel path depressions measured in inches, indicating structural distress.
Total length of the pavement section in miles.
Average width of paved shoulder in feet.
Severity level of pavement shoving or rippling, typically near intersections.
Measurement of pavement surface friction and skid resistance.
reference: ASTM E274 - Standard Test Method for Skid Resistance

description: Type of pavement surface material for the assessed section.
Ambient air temperature in degrees Fahrenheit at the time of inspection.
Total linear feet of transverse cracks perpendicular to the pavement centerline.
Priority level for implementing the recommended pavement treatment.
Average number of trucks per day traveling on this pavement section over a one-year period.
Designation of whether the pavement section is located in an urban or rural area.
Reference identifier linking to video log footage of the pavement section.
Weather conditions at the time of pavement inspection.
Number of years elapsed since the last overlay or resurfacing treatment.
Unique identifier for the pavement section within the highway system. Primary key for the pavement section master entity.

Foreign key linking to gis.feature. Business justification: Pavement sections have defined geographic boundaries for maintenance planning and asset management. GIS feature provides spatial extent for work zone planning and material quantity calculations.

Foreign key linking to highway.segment. Business justification: Pavement sections are linear subdivisions of highway segments for pavement management purposes. Each pavement section belongs to exactly one segment, defined by route and milepost range. Adding segmen
Annual Average Daily Traffic volume representing the total volume of vehicle traffic on the pavement section for a year divided by 365 days. Key metric for pavement loading and deterioration.
Year for which the AADT value was calculated or estimated.
Percentage of pavement section area affected by alligator (fatigue) cracking. Interconnected cracks forming a pattern resembling alligator skin, indicating structural failure.
Thickness of the base course layer measured in inches. Provides structural support and load distribution.
reference: AASHTO Guide for Design of Pavement Structures

description: Starting milepost location of the pavement section along the route. Measured in miles from route origin.

North Carolina climate zone classification for the pavement section location. Affects pavement design parameters and deterioration rates. COASTAL=eastern coastal plain, PIEDMONT=central region, MOUNTAIN=western mountains.
Actual construction cost in US dollars for building or rehabilitating this pavement section. Includes materials, labor, and equipment.
Specific date when the pavement section construction was completed and opened to traffic.
Year when the pavement section was originally constructed. Used for age-based deterioration modeling and lifecycle analysis.
Name of the contractor who constructed or performed major rehabilitation on this pavement section.
North Carolina county code where the pavement section is located. Used for geographic and administrative reporting.
Overall severity rating of pavement cracking distresses including alligator cracking, longitudinal cracking, and transverse cracking. Ranges from NONE to SEVERE.
Source system or database from which the pavement section data was obtained (e.g., Agile Assets, TIMS, HiCAMS).
Area under the deflection basin curve measured during Falling Weight Deflectometer testing. Indicates overall pavement structural capacity and remaining life.
Expected design life of the pavement structure in years. Typically 20 years for flexible pavements and 30-40 years for rigid pavements.
reference: AASHTO Guide for Design of Pavement Structures

description: Total design thickness of the pavement structure measured in inches, including all layers from surface to subgrade.
reference: AASHTO Guide for Design of Pavement Structures

description: NCDOT Division of Highways division number responsible for maintenance and operations of this pavement section. North Carolina has 14 highway divisions.
Rating of the pavement drainage system effectiveness. Good drainage is critical for pavement performance and longevity.
reference: AASHTO Guide for Design of Pavement Structures

description: Ending milepost location of the pavement section along the route. Measured in miles from route origin.

business_glossary_term: National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) Clearance Type
description: Type of NEPA environmental clearance obtained for the pavement project. CE=Categorical Exclusion, EA=Environmental Assessment, EIS=Environmental Impact Statement, FONSI=Finding of No Significant Impact.

business_glossary_term: Equivalent Single Axle Load (ESAL) Design Value
description: Design traffic loading expressed as cumulative 18,000-pound equivalent single axle loads over the pavement design life. Used for structural pavement design.
reference: AASHTO Guide for Design of Pavement Structures

description: Estimated cost in US dollars to perform the recommended pavement treatment. Based on unit costs and section characteristics.
Difference in elevation across concrete pavement joints measured in inches. Applicable to rigid pavements only. Caused by pumping and erosion of base materials.
Specific federal aid program providing funding for this pavement section (e.g., NHPP, STP, HSIP, CMAQ). Applicable only for federally funded projects.
Skid resistance measurement representing the friction between vehicle tires and pavement surface. Critical for safety. Measured using standardized friction testing equipment.
Date when the most recent pavement friction testing was performed.
Expected depth of frost penetration into the pavement structure and subgrade measured in inches. Critical for pavement design in freeze-thaw climates.
reference: AASHTO Guide for Design of Pavement Structures

description: FHWA functional classification code indicating the role of the roadway in serving mobility versus land access. Ranges from 1 (Interstate) to 9 (Local).
Descriptive name of the functional classification (e.g., Interstate, Principal Arterial, Minor Collector, Local).
Primary source of funding for the pavement construction or rehabilitation. STATE=state funds only, FEDERAL=federal funds, LOCAL=local funds, MIXED=combination of sources.
Latitude coordinate of the pavement section midpoint in decimal degrees. Used for spatial analysis and mapping.
Longitude coordinate of the pavement section midpoint in decimal degrees. Used for spatial analysis and mapping.

business_glossary_term: Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Sample Indicator
description: Flag indicating whether this pavement section is part of the HPMS sample for federal reporting. HPMS sample sections require more detailed data collection and reporting.
Date when the IRI measurement was collected using automated pavement condition survey equipment.
International Roughness Index measured in inches per mile. Quantifies pavement roughness and ride quality. Lower values indicate smoother pavement. Typical range 40-200 inches/mile.
Average width of a single traffic lane measured in feet. Standard lane widths range from 10 to 12 feet.
Date of the most recent pavement condition inspection or survey.
Timestamp when the pavement section record was last updated in the system.
Date when the construction contract for this pavement section was let (awarded) to a contractor. Key milestone in project delivery.
Percentage of load transferred across joints or cracks in rigid pavements. Measured using deflection testing. Higher values indicate better load transfer and structural performance.
Total linear feet of longitudinal cracking parallel to the pavement centerline. Often occurs along construction joints or wheel paths.
Maintenance unit or crew responsible for routine maintenance activities on this pavement section.
Type of median separating opposing traffic directions. NONE=undivided, PAINTED=painted centerline only, RAISED=raised median, BARRIER=concrete barrier, DEPRESSED=depressed median.
Width of the median measured in feet from edge of traveled way to edge of traveled way. Applicable only for divided highways.
Scheduled date for the next pavement condition inspection or survey based on inspection frequency requirements.
Flag indicating whether this pavement section is part of the National Highway System, which includes roadways important to the nation's economy, defense, and mobility.
Tire-pavement noise level measured in decibels using on-board sound intensity method. Lower values indicate quieter pavement surfaces.
Free-text field for additional notes, comments, or special conditions related to the pavement section that do not fit in structured fields.
Total number of through traffic lanes in both directions for this pavement section. Does not include auxiliary lanes, turn lanes, or shoulders.
Composite overall condition rating of the pavement section based on multiple distress indicators and performance measures. Used for prioritization and decision-making.
Percentage of pavement section area that has been patched or repaired. Indicates previous maintenance activity and potential for future deterioration.
Age of the pavement section in years since original construction or last major rehabilitation. Used for deterioration modeling and lifecycle analysis.
Classification of the pavement structural design. FLEXIBLE=asphalt layers on aggregate base, RIGID=concrete slab, COMPOSITE=asphalt overlay on concrete base.
reference: AASHTO Guide for Design of Pavement Structures

description: Date when the PCI rating was determined through visual distress survey or automated assessment.
Pavement Condition Index rating on a scale of 0 to 100, where 100 represents excellent condition and 0 represents failed pavement. Composite measure based on distress type, severity, and extent.
Rating of pavement surface permeability to water infiltration. Affects durability and moisture-related distresses. Permeable pavements allow water to drain through the surface.
NCDOT project number associated with the construction or major rehabilitation of this pavement section. Links to project management and financial systems.
Present Serviceability Index rating on a scale of 0 to 5, where 5 represents excellent pavement condition and 0 represents failed pavement. Subjective measure of pavement ride quality.
reference: AASHTO Guide for Design of Pavement Structures

description: Type of pavement treatment recommended based on current condition and deterioration modeling. Categories align with NCDOT pavement preservation strategies.
Fiscal year when the recommended pavement treatment should be performed based on condition forecasting and budget optimization.
Estimated remaining service life in years before the pavement reaches terminal condition requiring major rehabilitation or reconstruction.
Maximum rut depth measured in inches in the wheel path. Rutting is a longitudinal depression in the pavement surface caused by consolidation or lateral movement of materials.
Total length of the pavement section measured in miles. Calculated as end_milepost minus begin_milepost.
Average width of the paved or unpaved shoulder measured in feet. Provides emergency stopping area and lateral support for pavement structure.

Current operational status of the pavement section. ACTIVE=in service, INACTIVE=temporarily closed, PLANNED=future construction, UNDER_CONSTRUCTION=currently being built, DECOMMISSIONED=removed from service.

business_glossary_term: State Transportation Improvement Program (STIP) Project Indicator
description: Flag indicating whether this pavement section is part of a project included in the North Carolina State Transportation Improvement Program.
AASHTO Structural Number representing the overall structural capacity of the pavement. Calculated from layer thicknesses and material coefficients. Higher values indicate stronger pavement structure.
reference: AASHTO Guide for Design of Pavement Structures

business_glossary_term: Subgrade Resilient Modulus in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI)
description: Resilient modulus of the subgrade soil measured in pounds per square inch. Represents the elastic stiffness of the subgrade under repeated loading. Key input for mechanistic pavement design.
reference: AASHTO Guide for Design of Pavement Structures

description: Classification of the subgrade soil type underlying the pavement structure. Affects bearing capacity and pavement design requirements.
Thickness of the surface course layer measured in inches. The wearing surface that provides skid resistance and smoothness.
Code representing the pavement surface type. AC=Asphalt Concrete, PCC=Portland Cement Concrete, COMP=Composite, UNPAVED=Gravel or Dirt, BRICK=Brick or Block, OTHER=Other surface types.
Detailed description of the pavement surface type and composition, including specific materials and construction methods used.
Mean texture depth of the pavement surface measured in millimeters. Affects skid resistance, noise, and splash/spray. Measured using sand patch or laser methods.
Number of transverse cracks perpendicular to the pavement centerline. Often caused by thermal contraction or reflection from underlying layers.
Numerical ranking of this pavement section for treatment priority within the network. Lower numbers indicate higher priority for maintenance or rehabilitation.

Percentage of total traffic volume consisting of trucks and heavy vehicles. Critical for pavement design and deterioration modeling as trucks cause significantly more pavement damage than passenger vehicles.
Classification of the pavement section location as urban, rural, or small urban area based on Census Bureau definitions and population density.
Date when the construction warranty period expires. Applicable only for warranty projects.
Flag indicating whether this pavement section was constructed under a warranty contract requiring the contractor to maintain performance standards for a specified period.
Primary key for the pavement_treatment association
Foreign key linking to the pavement section receiving treatment
Foreign key linking to the transportation project that delivered the treatment
Actual date when the treatment work was completed and the pavement section was reopened to traffic.

Specific date when the most recent overlay or resurfacing treatment was completed. [Moved from pavement_section: This attribute represents the most recent overlay treatment date, which should be derived from the pavement_treatment association rather than stored redundantly on pavement_section.]

Year when the most recent overlay or resurfacing treatment was applied to the pavement section. Specific date when the most recent major rehabilitation work was completed. [Moved from pavement_section: This attribute represents the most recent rehabilitation treatment date, which should be derived from the pavement_treatment association rather than stored redundantly on pavement_section.]

Year when the most recent major rehabilitation work was performed on the pavement section, including reconstruction or major structural improvements. [Moved from pavement_section: This attribute represents the most recent rehabilitation treatment, which should be derived from the pavement_treatment association rather than stored redundantly on pavement_section.]
Pavement condition index or rating assessed after the treatment was completed. Used to measure treatment effectiveness and expected service life extension.
Pavement condition index or rating assessed before the treatment was applied. Used to establish baseline condition and justify treatment selection.
Planned date for the treatment work to be performed on this pavement section as part of the project schedule.
Classification of the pavement treatment work performed. Identifies the specific maintenance or rehabilitation strategy applied to the section.
Detailed description of the specific work performed on this pavement section, including materials used, layer thicknesses, and any special treatments or conditions.
Unique identifier for the roadway functional classification record. Primary key for the roadway classification reference table.

Level of access control typically associated with this functional classification. Full access control means access only at interchanges; partial means limited access points; none means unrestricted access.
reference: AASHTO Green Book, FHWA Access Management Guidelines

description: Current status of this functional classification code in the reference table. Inactive or deprecated codes are retained for historical reporting.
Policy requirement for bicycle accommodation on roadways in this functional classification.
reference: NCDOT Complete Streets Policy, AASHTO Guide for Development of Bicycle Facilities

description: Standard interval in months between bridge inspections for bridges on roadways in this functional classification, per NBIS requirements.
reference: 23 CFR 650 Subpart C - National Bridge Inspection Standards (NBIS)

description: Approximate percentage of total state highway system centerline miles represented by roadways in this functional classification.

business_glossary_term: Congestion Mitigation and Air Quality (CMAQ) Eligible Flag
description: Indicates whether roadways with this functional classification are eligible for Congestion Mitigation and Air Quality improvement program funding.
Indicates whether roadways in this functional classification are subject to federal congestion monitoring and reporting requirements.
reference: 23 CFR 490 Subpart E - National Performance Management Measures for Congestion

business_glossary_term: Maximum Design Speed in Miles Per Hour
description: Maximum design speed in miles per hour typically associated with this functional classification, based on AASHTO design standards.
reference: AASHTO Green Book - A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets

business_glossary_term: Minimum Design Speed in Miles Per Hour
description: Minimum design speed in miles per hour typically associated with this functional classification, based on AASHTO design standards.
reference: AASHTO Green Book - A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets

description: Date when this functional classification definition became effective for use in NCDOT systems and reporting.
Typical level of environmental review required under NEPA for projects on roadways in this functional classification.
Date when this functional classification definition was superseded or deprecated. Null for currently active classifications.
Indicates whether roadways with this functional classification are eligible for federal aid funding programs administered by FHWA.
Date when this functional classification was approved by FHWA for use in federal reporting and funding programs.
Standard abbreviated form of the functional classification name used in reporting and mapping (e.g., INT, PA, MA, MC, LOC).
Numeric code representing the functional classification of the roadway as defined by FHWA. Standard codes include 1 (Interstate), 2 (Principal Arterial), 6 (Minor Collector), etc.
Full descriptive name of the functional classification (e.g., Interstate, Principal Arterial - Other Freeways and Expressways, Minor Arterial, Major Collector, Local).
Numeric ranking of the functional classification in the roadway hierarchy, with 1 being highest (Interstate) and 7 being lowest (Local). Used for network analysis and routing.

business_glossary_term: Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Reporting Required Flag
description: Indicates whether roadways with this functional classification must be reported in the annual HPMS submission to FHWA.

business_glossary_term: Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Sample Panel Flag
description: Indicates whether roadways with this functional classification are included in the HPMS sample panel for detailed data collection.

business_glossary_term: Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) Eligible Flag
description: Indicates whether roadways with this functional classification are eligible for Highway Safety Improvement Program funding.
Priority level for deployment of Intelligent Transportation Systems infrastructure on roadways in this functional classification.
reference: FHWA ITS Deployment Guidelines, NCDOT ITS Strategic Plan

description: Percentage emphasis on land access versus mobility for this functional classification. Higher values indicate greater emphasis on providing access to adjacent properties.
Date when this functional classification definition was last reviewed and validated by NCDOT planning staff.
Typical governmental entity or organization responsible for maintenance of roadways in this functional classification.
reference: NCGS Chapter 136, NCDOT Maintenance Operations Manual

description: Typical median configuration for roadways in this functional classification (divided with physical median, undivided, or variable).
reference: AASHTO Green Book, NCDOT Roadway Design Manual

description: Percentage emphasis on mobility (movement of traffic) versus land access for this functional classification. Higher values indicate greater emphasis on mobility.
Indicates whether roadways with this functional classification are eligible for inclusion in the National Highway System. NHS designation affects federal funding and reporting requirements.
Additional notes, clarifications, or special considerations related to this functional classification.
Indicates whether roadways in this functional classification are typically eligible for oversize/overweight permit routing.
Standard frequency for pavement condition monitoring and assessment for roadways in this functional classification.
reference: AASHTO Pavement Management Guide, NCDOT PMS Guidelines

business_glossary_term: Pavement Performance Target Pavement Condition Index (PCI)
description: Target Pavement Condition Index score for roadways in this functional classification, used for asset management and performance measurement.
reference: AASHTO Transportation Asset Management Guide, NCDOT PMS

description: Policy requirement for pedestrian accommodation (sidewalks, crosswalks) on roadways in this functional classification.
reference: NCDOT Complete Streets Policy, ADA Standards, AASHTO Guide for Planning, Designing, and Operating Pedestrian Facilities

business_glossary_term: Typical Posted Speed Limit Maximum in Miles Per Hour
description: Typical maximum posted speed limit in miles per hour for roadways in this functional classification.
reference: NCGS 20-141, MUTCD, NCDOT Speed Zone Guidelines

business_glossary_term: Typical Posted Speed Limit Minimum in Miles Per Hour
description: Typical minimum posted speed limit in miles per hour for roadways in this functional classification.
reference: NCGS 20-141, MUTCD, NCDOT Speed Zone Guidelines

description: Detailed description of the primary transportation function served by roadways in this classification (e.g., long-distance travel, regional connectivity, local access).
Typical right-of-way width in feet for roadways in this functional classification, based on NCDOT design standards.
reference: NCDOT Roadway Design Manual, AASHTO Green Book

description: Indicates whether roadways in this functional classification are included in safety performance monitoring and Highway Safety Improvement Program analysis.

business_glossary_term: State Transportation Improvement Program (STIP) Eligible Flag
description: Indicates whether roadways with this functional classification are eligible for inclusion in the State Transportation Improvement Program for project funding.
Indicates whether roadways with this functional classification are eligible for Surface Transportation Program funding.
Indicates whether MUTCD traffic signal warrants typically apply to intersections on roadways in this functional classification.
reference: MUTCD Chapter 4C - Traffic Control Signal Needs Studies

description: Indicates whether roadways in this functional classification are typically eligible for designation as truck routes.
reference: 23 CFR 658, NCGS 20-116, NCDOT Truck Route Guidelines

business_glossary_term: Typical Annual Average Daily Traffic (AADT) Range Maximum
description: Maximum typical Annual Average Daily Traffic volume expected for roadways in this functional classification. Used for planning and classification validation.
reference: AASHTO Green Book, FHWA Traffic Monitoring Guide

business_glossary_term: Typical Annual Average Daily Traffic (AADT) Range Minimum
description: Minimum typical Annual Average Daily Traffic volume expected for roadways in this functional classification. Used for planning and classification validation.
reference: AASHTO Green Book, FHWA Traffic Monitoring Guide

description: Typical number of through lanes (both directions combined) for roadways in this functional classification.
reference: AASHTO Green Book, NCDOT Roadway Design Manual

description: Typical width of travel lanes in feet for roadways in this functional classification, per AASHTO design standards.
reference: AASHTO Green Book, NCDOT Roadway Design Manual

description: Typical shoulder width in feet for roadways in this functional classification, per AASHTO design standards.
reference: AASHTO Green Book, NCDOT Roadway Design Manual

description: Average trip length in miles for trips using roadways in this functional classification. Used for travel demand modeling and planning.
Indicates whether this functional classification applies to urban areas, rural areas, or both. Critical for HPMS reporting and federal funding eligibility.
Approximate percentage of statewide Vehicle Miles Traveled contributed by roadways in this functional classification. Used for system performance analysis.
reference: FHWA HPMS, NCDOT Traffic Survey Unit

description: Primary key for route

Level of access control limiting entry and exit points along the route. Full control (interstates) allows access only at interchanges; partial control limits driveways and intersections; no control allows unrestricted access.
Average number of vehicles traveling on the route per day over a one-year period. Critical metric for capacity planning, safety analysis, pavement design, and funding allocation.
Starting milepost reference point for the route. Typically 0.000 for route origin but may vary for route segments or realignments.
Free-text field for additional notes, special conditions, historical information, or operational considerations related to the route that do not fit in structured fields.
Year the route was originally constructed and opened to traffic. Used for historical analysis and asset age tracking.
Primary directional orientation or traffic flow direction of the route. Used for route identification and traffic management purposes.
Date when the current route designation, classification, or configuration became effective. Used for temporal tracking and historical analysis of route changes.
Indicates whether the route is designated as an emergency evacuation route for natural disasters or other emergency situations. Affects maintenance priorities and emergency response planning.
Ending milepost reference point for the route. Represents the terminal point of the route within the state system.
FHWA functional classification code indicating the role of the route in the highway network hierarchy. Used for federal funding eligibility and performance monitoring requirements.
Date of the most recent major resurfacing or pavement rehabilitation project on the route. Used for lifecycle analysis and maintenance scheduling.

Entity responsible for routine and major maintenance activities on the route. May differ from ownership in cases of maintenance agreements. DOH (Department of Highways) indicates NCDOT state maintenance responsibility.
Type of median separation between opposing traffic flows. Critical safety feature affecting crash rates and access management.

Indicates whether the route is part of the National Highway System, a network of strategic highways important to the nation's economy, defense, and mobility. NHS designation affects federal funding eligibility and performance monitoring requirements.
Total number of through traffic lanes in both directions for the route. Excludes auxiliary lanes, turn lanes, and shoulders. Used for capacity analysis and safety assessments.

URL of a web page providing additional information about the specific stop, such as real-time arrival information or amenities.
Indicates whether wheelchair boarding is possible at this stop. Supports ADA compliance tracking and rider accessibility planning.
reference: GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification), ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act)

description: The postal ZIP code for the transit stop location. Supports demographic analysis and service area planning.
Unique identifier for the ticket transaction record. Primary key for the ticket entity.
Identifier of the employee or agent who processed the ticket sale. Used for ticket office and call center transactions.
Identifier of the device or terminal where the ticket was validated (fare box, gate reader, handheld validator).

Foreign key linking to finance.payment. Business justification: Each ticket purchase generates a payment transaction that must be recorded in the financial system. Finance uses this to reconcile daily ticket sales revenue with bank deposits.
Identifier of the point-of-sale terminal or ticket vending machine where the transaction occurred.

Foreign key linking to transit.rider. Business justification: Ticket must reference the rider who purchased or validated it. The rider_id FK does not currently exist in ticket schema and must be added. This normalizes rider_category (eligibility type), rider_nam
Indicates whether the rider requires accessible vehicle or service accommodations under ADA requirements.
Barcode or QR code value printed on the ticket for validation and scanning purposes.
Date and time when the reservation was made, in format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX. May differ from purchase_timestamp for advance bookings.
Reason code or description for ticket cancellation (customer request, service disruption, weather, system error, etc.).
Date and time when the ticket was cancelled, in format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX. Null for active tickets.
Number of companions or personal care attendants traveling with the rider. Relevant for paratransit and accessible services.
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the transaction. Typically USD for NCDOT operations.
Ending location or station for the trip associated with the ticket. For ferry tickets, this is the arrival terminal. For transit, this is the alighting stop or station.
Total discount applied to the base fare amount, including promotional discounts, senior/student reductions, or subsidy programs. Denominated in US dollars.
Date and time when the ticket expires and is no longer valid for use, in format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
Base fare amount charged for the ticket before any discounts, taxes, or fees. Denominated in US dollars.
Pricing category applied to the ticket, indicating whether full fare, reduced fare, or special pricing was applied.
Additional fees charged for the ticket transaction, such as processing fees, convenience fees, or service charges. Denominated in US dollars.
Primary funding source or grant program supporting the transit service associated with the ticket. Critical for FTA grant compliance and reporting.
Name of the MPO or RPO (Rural Planning Organization) jurisdiction where the service operates. Used for regional transit planning and coordination.
Free-text notes or comments about the ticket transaction, including special accommodations, customer requests, or operational notes.
Human-readable ticket number displayed to riders and used for customer service reference. May include alphanumeric formatting specific to transit system or ferry service.
Standardized code identifying the transit agency or ferry operator. Used for FTA reporting and inter-agency coordination.
Name of the transit agency or ferry operator providing the service. NCDOT coordinates with multiple transit systems and operates ferry services.
Starting location or station for the trip associated with the ticket. For ferry tickets, this is the departure terminal. For transit, this is the boarding stop or station.
Number of passengers covered by the ticket. Typically 1 for individual tickets, may be greater for group tickets or vehicle tickets that include driver and passengers.
Interface or location where the ticket was purchased, indicating the customer touchpoint used for the transaction.
Promotional or discount code applied to the ticket purchase for marketing campaigns or special offers.
Date and time when the ticket was purchased or issued, in format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
Unique receipt number issued for the transaction, used for accounting reconciliation and customer service.
Amount refunded to the customer for cancelled or unused tickets. Denominated in US dollars.
Date and time when the refund was processed, in format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
Unique reservation identifier for advance-booking services such as ferry reservations or paratransit trips.
Descriptive name of the transit route or ferry service associated with the ticket.
Transit route number or ferry route identifier associated with the ticket. May be null for system-wide passes.
Geographic service area or region covered by the ticket (county, city, regional district).
Mode of transportation service provided by the ticket, indicating the type of transit or ferry service.
Unique identifier of the smart card or fare media used for the ticket. Used for contactless payment systems and reloadable fare cards.
Description of special accommodations requested or provided (wheelchair, service animal, mobility device, etc.).
Current lifecycle status of the ticket, indicating whether it is available for use, has been used, or is no longer valid.
Dollar amount of subsidy applied to the ticket from federal, state, or local assistance programs. Denominated in US dollars.
Name of the subsidy or assistance program applied to the ticket fare (senior discount program, low-income assistance, employer subsidy, etc.).
Total tax amount applied to the ticket transaction. Denominated in US dollars.
Total amount paid for the ticket including base fare, taxes, fees, and after discounts. Denominated in US dollars.
External payment processor or financial system reference number for the transaction, used for reconciliation and dispute resolution.
Indicates whether the ticket allows transfers to other routes or services within the validity period.
Number of transfers allowed or used with this ticket. May be null for unlimited transfer passes.
Scheduled date of travel for the ticket, in format yyyy-MM-dd. For single-ride tickets with specific trip reservations.
Scheduled departure time for the trip. For ferry reservations and scheduled transit services.

Classification of the ticket product purchased, indicating fare category and validity period. Includes both transit and ferry ticket types as this product consolidates ferry.ticket and transit.ticket.
Start date of the ticket validity period, in format yyyy-MM-dd. For passes and multi-day tickets.
End date of the ticket validity period, in format yyyy-MM-dd. For passes and multi-day tickets.
Physical location where the ticket was validated (station name, vehicle number, terminal).
Date and time when the ticket was first validated or activated for use, in format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX. May be null for unused tickets.
Length of vehicle being transported on ferry, measured in feet. Used for ferry capacity planning and fare calculation for oversized vehicles.
Type of vehicle being transported on ferry service. Primarily applicable to ferry tickets. Null for transit-only tickets.
Fare zone identifier for the destination location. Used in zone-based fare systems.
Fare zone identifier for the origin location. Used in zone-based fare systems.
Unique identifier for the transit schedule record. Primary key for the transit schedule entity.
Identifier for the block of trips that a single vehicle operates. Used for vehicle and operator scheduling.
Identifier for the fare structure applicable to this scheduled service.

business_glossary_term: GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) Feed Identifier
description: Identifier for the GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) data feed containing this schedule information.
Identifier for the transit operator or agency providing the scheduled service.
Identifier for the transit route to which this schedule applies. Links schedule to specific route definition.
Identifier for the RPO (Rural Planning Organization) jurisdiction where the scheduled service operates.
Identifier for the service pattern (e.g., weekday, weekend, holiday) that defines when this schedule is active.
Identifier for the MPO (Metropolitan Planning Organization) jurisdiction where the scheduled service operates.
reference: FHWA (Federal Highway Administration) MPO (Metropolitan Planning Organization) Standards

description: Unique identifier for a specific trip within the schedule. A trip represents one vehicle traveling along a route.

business_glossary_term: ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act) Compliance Indicator
description: Indicates whether the scheduled service meets ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act) compliance requirements.
Date when the schedule was officially approved by the transit authority or governing body.
Name or identifier of the person or authority who approved the schedule.
Indicates whether bicycles are allowed on the scheduled trip.
Specific date when service differs from the regular schedule (e.g., holidays, special events).
Reason for schedule cancellation or suspension (e.g., weather, maintenance, low ridership).
Email address for schedule inquiries and customer service.
Phone number for schedule inquiries and customer service.
Description of coordination with other transit services, including transfer points and connecting routes.
Direction of travel for the trip (e.g., inbound, outbound, northbound).
Date when this schedule expires and service ends.
Indicates whether the scheduled service meets environmental compliance requirements under NEPA (National Environmental Policy Act) and state regulations.
Type of exception applied on the calendar exception date (service added, removed, or modified).
Base fare amount charged for the scheduled trip.
Currency code for the fare amount (ISO 4217 standard).
Time of the first scheduled departure for the service day in HH:MM:SS format.
Indicates whether service operates on exact scheduled times or frequency-based intervals.
Indicates whether service operates on Fridays under this schedule.
Specific FTA (Federal Transit Administration) grant program funding this scheduled service (e.g., Section 5307, 5311, 5339).
Primary funding source for the scheduled transit service (federal, state, local, or fare revenue).
Time interval in minutes between consecutive vehicle departures on the route during scheduled service.
Time of the last scheduled departure for the service day in HH:MM:SS format.
Date when the schedule record was last modified or updated.
Indicates whether service operates on Mondays under this schedule.
Additional notes or comments about the schedule, including special instructions or service alerts.
Time interval in minutes between consecutive vehicle departures during off-peak service hours.
Name of the transit operator or agency providing the scheduled service.
Time when peak service period ends in HH:MM:SS format.
Time interval in minutes between consecutive vehicle departures during peak service hours.
Time when peak service period begins in HH:MM:SS format.
Date when the schedule was published and made available to the public.
Indicates whether real-time service updates are available for this schedule.
Public-facing name or number of the transit route (e.g., Route 15, Blue Line Express).
Indicates whether service operates on Saturdays under this schedule.
Geographic classification of the service area (urban, rural, suburban, or regional).
Descriptive name for the service pattern (e.g., Weekday Service, Saturday Service, Holiday Service).
Type of transit service provided (e.g., fixed route, demand response, express).
Date when this schedule becomes effective and service begins.
Current operational status of the schedule (active, inactive, suspended, planned, or cancelled).
Indicates whether service operates on Sundays under this schedule.
Indicates whether service operates on Thursdays under this schedule.
Indicates whether service operates on Tuesdays under this schedule.
Maximum passenger capacity of the vehicle assigned to the scheduled trip.
Type of vehicle used for the scheduled service.
Version number or identifier for the schedule publication, used to track schedule changes over time.

business_glossary_term: Schedule Information Website URL (Uniform Resource Locator)
description: Website URL (Uniform Resource Locator) where schedule information is published for public access.
Indicates whether service operates on Wednesdays under this schedule.
Indicates whether the scheduled trip is wheelchair accessible per ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act) requirements.
Unique identifier for a specific transit trip instance. Primary key for the trip entity.
Identifies the block of sequential trips assigned to the same vehicle and operator during a service period.
Indicates the direction of travel for the trip. 0 = outbound/one direction, 1 = inbound/opposite direction.

Foreign key linking to hr.employee. Business justification: Transit trips require assigned drivers who are NCDOT employees. Operations dispatch uses this daily to track which employee operated each trip for payroll, compliance, and incident management.
Identifier for the geographic path/alignment that the vehicle follows for this trip.
Identifier for the transit route on which this trip operates. Links to the route master data.

Identifier for the RPO jurisdiction in which this trip operates, if applicable.
Identifier for the service calendar pattern (weekday, weekend, holiday schedule) under which this trip operates.
Identifier for the MPO jurisdiction in which this trip operates, if applicable.
Identifier for the transit agency or operator responsible for providing this trip service.
Actual duration of the trip in minutes from first stop departure to last stop arrival.
Actual arrival time at the final stop of the trip as recorded by AVL (Automatic Vehicle Location) or operator.
Actual departure time from the first stop of the trip as recorded by AVL (Automatic Vehicle Location) or operator.
Total number of passenger alightings (exits) across all stops during this trip.
Indicates whether AVL tracking was active and recording location data for this trip.
Indicates whether bicycles are allowed on this trip. 0 = no information, 1 = allowed, 2 = not allowed.
Total number of passenger boardings across all stops during this trip.
Reason code or description explaining why the trip was cancelled, if applicable.
Timestamp when the trip record was initially created in the system.
Miles traveled while the vehicle is not in revenue service (e.g., traveling to/from garage, repositioning).
Number of minutes the trip was delayed relative to the scheduled time. Negative values indicate early arrival.
Descriptive name for the direction of travel (e.g., 'Northbound', 'To Downtown', 'Eastbound').
Reason code or description explaining why the trip was diverted from its normal route, if applicable.
Estimated carbon dioxide emissions produced during this trip, measured in kilograms.
Fare category or pricing tier applicable to this trip (e.g., 'standard', 'express', 'premium').
Total fare revenue collected from passengers during this trip.
FTA grant number under which this trip service is funded, if applicable.
Amount of fuel consumed by the vehicle during this trip, measured in gallons.
Type of fuel or energy source used by the vehicle for this trip.
Primary funding source category for this trip service (FTA grant, state appropriation, local funding, etc.).
Text displayed on the vehicle headsign to identify the trip destination to passengers.
Indicates whether any safety or operational incident occurred during this trip.
Classification of the incident that occurred during the trip (e.g., 'accident', 'breakdown', 'passenger injury').
Timestamp when the trip record was last updated or modified.
Maximum number of passengers on board the vehicle at any point during the trip (peak load point).
